title: bug: DEAD team members keep their team seats until the 30-min stale prune, so seats launched after a fleet restart run teamless and skip claimable rows
description:
Observed 2026-10-30, filed by governor-4764040b.

What happened:
- At 20:23Z the JetBrains plugin deregistered 16 seats with terminal_closed. Each became DEAD and its record was kept.
- Worker team team-a94dc136 ("moes", maxSize 20) kept all 16 in memberIds, so it stayed full at 20/20.
- Three seats launched after 20:24Z could not join: worker-632cd3f0, architect-915213a1 and architect-4ff0711c. The wrapper warned "moe.join_team refused: ... this seat has NO team, so claim_next_task skips every epic a live worker already holds".
- worker-632cd3f0 was alive and polling every 30s. It still never claimed WT-04 (task-c20464ff). From 20:34Z WT-04 was the only claimable WORKING row and the head of the 28-row critical chain. It was skipped because worker-c0a1ac70 held WT-08T in the same epic and status.
- At 20:42Z the governor removed the 16 DEAD members with moe.leave_team. The seat joined and claimed WT-04 within 5s.

Mechanism, as read from the code:
- packages/moe-daemon/src/state/teamStore.ts addTeamMember refuses when `existing.memberIds.length >= existing.maxSize`, and that count includes DEAD members.
- Membership is dropped, with a formerMemberIds tombstone, only by deleteWorker (state/workerStore.ts).
- deleteWorker runs from the stale-worker sweep (state/sweeps.ts, Layer 3) once staleWorkerTimeoutMs (30 min) has passed, or at a restart purge.
- Deregistration (moe.deregister_worker, the plugin's DEREGISTER_WORKER) marks the record DEAD and leaves its membership.
- So after any IDE tab-close wave, new seats run teamless for up to about 35 minutes.

Constraint: a hot reload deregisters with wrapper_restart and re-registers under the SAME id (every seat did this at 19:53Z). A DEAD member re-joining under its own id must keep working.

The fix is the planner's call. For example: count only non-DEAD members against maxSize, and on a join, evict the DEAD members to formerMemberIds the way deleteWorker does. The teamless claim filter itself is out of scope.
definitionOfDone: Daemon regression test, RED on the parent: a team at maxSize whose members include DEAD workers accepts join_team from a new worker, and the team never holds more than maxSize non-DEAD members.
A DEAD member re-joining under its own id (the wrapper_restart path) still succeeds when the team is otherwise full.
Evicted DEAD members land in formerMemberIds, as deleteWorker does, and the teamless claim filter is unchanged.

Tests first (RED). Create packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/joinTeam.deadMembers.test.ts.

Model the harness on tools/joinTeam.notification.test.ts:
- `const h = new ToolTestHarness()`; beforeEach runs `h.init(); h.setupMoeFolder(); await h.state.load()`; afterEach runs `vi.restoreAllMocks(); h.cleanup()`.
- Calls go through the tool handlers: joinTeamTool(h.state).handler({ teamId, workerId }, h.state), and deregisterWorkerTool(h.state).handler({ workerId, reason }, h.state).
- Helper live(team): the memberIds whose record is not DEAD.
- After EVERY successful join, assert live(team).length <= team.maxSize and memberIds.length <= team.maxSize. This is DoD 1's "never more than maxSize non-DEAD members".

Use exact arrays and exact fields, never bare truthiness.

(1) DoD 1, RED on the parent.
    - Setup: team maxSize 3; join w-a, w-b and w-c; deregister w-a and w-b with reason 'terminal_closed'; snapshot both records.
    - join('w-new') resolves.

(3) DoD 2, the wrapper_restart path.
    - Setup: maxSize 2; join w-x and w-live; deregister w-x with 'wrapper_restart'.
    - join('w-x') resolves; memberIds toEqual ['w-x','w-live'], unchanged.
    - w-x has status 'IDLE'; w-live's record is deep-equal to before; formerMemberIds is absent or [].
    - Then join('w-other') rejects /is full/.
(4) DoD 3: tombstone parity with deleteWorker, and the claim filter is unchanged.
    - After (1)'s eviction, resolveEffectiveTeam(h.state, 'w-a')?.id equals the team id. That is the claim filter's own resolver, from util/teamMembershipHeal.ts, which stays untouched.

(5) A team below maxSize never evicts.
    - Setup: maxSize 3; w-a DEAD and w-b live.
    - join('w-c') gives memberIds ['w-a','w-b','w-c'], with no tombstone. That is today's behavior.

implementationPlan.description:
Fix addTeamMember in packages/moe-daemon/src/state/teamStore.ts.

(a) Keep the already-a-member early return first and unchanged. A DEAD member re-joining under its own id (wrapper_restart) keeps its seat (DoD 2), and joinTeam's handler then revives it to IDLE as today.

(b) Replace the full check:
    - When memberIds.length >= maxSize: let dead = the memberIds whose record exists with status 'DEAD'.
    - If memberIds.length - dead.length >= maxSize, throw the SAME Error(`Team ${name} is full (max ${maxSize} members)`) BEFORE any write. The wrappers and the existing tests match that text, and a refused join stays write-free. That ordering is the existing "refuse a full team BEFORE clearing the tombstone" rule.
    - Otherwise call a new local helper, evictDeadMembers(state, team, dead).
    - A team below maxSize never evicts: today's behavior, byte for byte.

(c) evictDeadMembers:
    - One state.updateTeam(team.id, { memberIds: memberIds minus dead, formerMemberIds: withEvictionTombstones(team, dead) }). This is the same tombstone deleteWorker writes. Import withEvictionTombstones from ../util/teamMembershipHeal.js; that module imports StateManager as a type only, so there is no runtime cycle.
    - For each evicted id whose record's teamId is this team: state.updateWorker(id, { teamId: null, lastActivityAt: worker.lastActivityAt }).
      - The record stays DEAD and keeps lastActivityAt, so the stale prune and presence stay accurate.
      - As after deleteWorker, the tombstone becomes its only membership trace.
      - Error handling: wrap each update in try/catch and log logger.warn({ err, workerId }, ...). Use the key `err`, not `error`, so pino serializes it. A failed pointer repair must never fail the join, because the team write already freed the seats.
    - For each id, state.appendActivity('TEAM_MEMBER_REMOVED', { teamId, workerId, reason: 'dead-member-evicted' }); then one logger.info naming the evicted ids.

(d) Then the existing clearMembershipTombstone, re-read, old-team cleanup and add flow runs unchanged. The re-read picks up the eviction.

(e) Add a short why-comment above the check: a DEAD record holds no seat, but it stays until staleWorkerTimeoutMs prunes it, so without this a tab-close wave left new seats teamless for about 35 min.

(f) In packages/moe-daemon/src/types/schema.ts, update the Team.formerMemberIds doc comment only: tombstones are also written when a join into a full team evicts DEAD members, whose records keep DEAD.

Do NOT change healTeamMembership, resolveEffectiveTeam, util/claimEligibility.ts or tools/claimNextTask.ts. DoD 3 requires the teamless claim filter to stay unchanged.

Then run the step-1 command with the fixed files overlaid too: all five cases pass.

Below-maxSize and already-a-member paths are byte-for-byte unchanged. schema.ts: Team.formerMemberIds doc comment only. Untouched: teamMembershipHeal.ts, claimEligibility.ts, claimNextTask.ts. Adversarial self-review of this task's own diff (`git diff -- <the 4 files>`), read as an attacker. Record the answers in the step note.

(1) Order: is any write done before the full-team refusal? The test-2 deep-equal pins this, but read the code too.

@architect-4ff0711c Planner input from the filer, measured on the live board. It's a related detail, not a DoD change.

teamStore.ts removeTeamMember calls `state.updateWorker(workerId, { teamId: null })` without passing lastActivityAt back, so the write counts as presence.
- Evidence: my 16 leave_team calls at 20:42:10-20:42:23Z bumped every DEAD record's lastActivityAt to those exact times (list_workers at 20:56Z).
- Effect: their stale prune moved from about 20:53Z to about 21:12Z.

If your fix evicts DEAD members at join time, keep that path from refreshing presence, or the evicted records outlive their prune by another staleWorkerTimeoutMs. Whether this goes into this row is your call.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Chosen: in addTeamMember, a non-member join that finds the team at maxSize evicts every DEAD member first. The eviction tombstones them to formerMemberIds with withEvictionTombstones, as deleteWorker does, and clears their teamId pointer with lastActivityAt kept. The join then counts only live members. Today's behavior is unchanged in every other state: below maxSize, a member re-joining, or a team full of live members.

Rejected:
(1) Always count only non-DEAD members and never evict. memberIds would grow past maxSize, which breaks validateTeamUpdates (memberIds.length <= maxSize) and every memberIds consumer.
(2) Evict only as many DEAD members as needed, oldest lastActivityAt first. That needs an ordering rule and buys nothing, because a non-member's join can evict a DEAD member that is mid-hot-reload only when live seats exceed maxSize, and then some live seat is teamless anyway. A reloading member that is not displaced re-joins idempotently. validateTeamUpdates keeps memberIds.length <= maxSize, so a full team needs exactly one seat.
(3) A 120 s grace before a DEAD member's seat frees. A literal reading of DoD 1 (just-deregistered members) would fail it, and (2)'s reasoning makes it unnecessary.
(4) Store the deregister reason on the Worker to tell wrapper_restart from terminal_closed. That is a schema change and unnecessary for the same reason.
(5) Also let healTeamMembership evict. The claim path is out of scope (DoD 3), and a tombstoned worker already counts as a member through resolveEffectiveTeam.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- addTeamMember (state/teamStore.ts) refuses at memberIds.length >= maxSize, counting DEAD members.
- deregisterWorker (state/workerLifecycle.ts) marks the record DEAD and keeps its membership. Only deleteWorker (stale prune / DEAD prune) and purgeAllWorkers drop membership, each tombstoning through withEvictionTombstones (util/teamMembershipHeal.ts).
- joinTeam's handler revives a DEAD joiner to IDLE after addTeamMember succeeds. Its already-a-member early return is the hot-reload re-join path.
- validateTeamUpdates rejects any update leaving memberIds.length > maxSize, so a full team is exactly full.
- updateWorker bumps lastActivityAt unless a value is passed. A DEAD record re-emits WORKER_DELETED.
- Every existing 'is full' test uses live members: joinTeam.notification.test.ts, workerType.test.ts, teamMembershipHeal.test.ts. They keep passing.
- A full daemon suite at HEAD 920f9cca in a native snapshot (node v24.21.0, env -i) gave 214 files, 6239 passed and 20 skipped, in 38 s including npm ci and tsc.

completionSummary: A join into a full team now evicts DEAD members first, so DEAD seats no longer hold a team at maxSize. addTeamMember (state/teamStore.ts) computes dead = memberIds whose record is DEAD and refuses with the unchanged `Team <name> is full (max N members)` only when live members fill maxSize, before any write. Otherwise the new local evictDeadMembers does one updateTeam (memberIds minus dead, formerMemberIds via withEvictionTombstones, the deleteWorker tombstone). It then clears teamId on each evicted record that points at this team, passing lastActivityAt back so the record stays DEAD and the repair is not presence. A failed pointer repair is logged and never fails the join. An existing member, including a DEAD one re-joining under its own id (wrapper_restart), still hits the idempotent early return and keeps its seat. A team below maxSize never evicts. A member with no worker record is not DEAD. Untouched: teamMembershipHeal.ts, claimEligibility.ts, claimNextTask.ts, MCP API, persisted fields. Also changed: Team.formerMemberIds doc comment (schema.ts) and the moe.join_team section of docs/MCP_SERVER.md. New joinTeam.deadMembers.test.ts has 7 cases; on the parent 4 fail with "is full" and 3 pin today's behavior. Mutants skip-tombstone, skip-teamId-reset and evict-below-maxSize were each killed. Not changed (outside approved scope): removeTeamMember still bumps a DEAD record's lastActivityAt (governor's planner input); noted in the handoff.

Approved. Reviewed completion 757dcce4 (on moe/work-2026-10-24, pushed, in task.commits); own non-board bytes ~+192 net (<400).

RED proof: with the parent's teamStore.ts in the snapshot, deadMembers.test.ts gives 4 failed (all `Team Workers is full (max 3 members)`) and 3 passed (the pin-today cases). Restored afterwards.

DoD 1: a full team with DEAD members accepts a new worker; live and total members stay <= maxSize after every join; a refused join leaves the team deep-equal (tests 1, 2).
DoD 2: a DEAD member re-joining under its own id (wrapper_restart) keeps its seat via the idempotent early return, is revived to IDLE, nothing is evicted, and the live peer is deep-equal (test 3).
DoD 3: evicted members land in formerMemberIds via withEvictionTombstones; records keep DEAD and lastActivityAt, teamId cleared; resolveEffectiveTeam still resolves them; a later deleteWorker leaves one tombstone (test 4). teamMembershipHeal.ts, claimEligibility.ts and claimNextTask.ts are not in the commit.

Code read: the full branch reads only until the throw, so nothing is written before the refusal; the error text is unchanged; a missing record is not DEAD; the teamId pointer is cleared only when it names this team, with an explicit lastActivityAt so it is not presence; a failed repair is logged and never fails the join. Joins run under the mutex (WebSocketServer.ts:887 and tool dispatch). Scope matches approvedScope.

Non-blocking: removeTeamMember (leave_team on a DEAD record) still bumps lastActivityAt; the architect scoped it out, so it needs its own row. healTeamMembership still skips a full team; the wrapper's join retry now evicts instead. Ponytail pass: nothing to cut.
